 Mixed Night in Europe For British Sides
 Europa League Archives | Written By James Capps | Published at October 16, 2026 Kyiv, Ukraine. 27 April 2025. Close-up of Celtic Football Club green jersey with embroidered logo and white star, detailed fabric texture. Last night, six British sides took to the pitch in the Europa League and Conference League group phases.
 It was almost a perfect night for the Premier League contingent, but it was another tough evening for their Scottish counterparts.
 Wins For Sunderland, Bournemouth and Brighton 
 We begin in the Europa League, where Sunderland and Bournemouth both made it two wins from two.
 The Cherries, celebrating their first home match in European competition, lived up to the occasion with a 3-0 win over Sturm Graz. Evanilson got them on the board just before half-time with a looping header that deceived visiting goalkeeper Daniil Khudyakov.
 The Austrians failed to create anything meaningful in front of goal and were duly punished by Rayan and Alvaro Rodriguez as Bournemouth ended the night fifth in the group-stage table.
 It was a trickier night for Sunderland, though, who needed a late winner from Noah Sadiki to beat Portuguese second-tier side Torreense.
 A wonder strike from Volnei put the hosts ahead, before two goals in the final 23 minutes spared Sunderland blushes.
 And in the Conference League, Brighton made light work of Lithuanian side Kauno Zalgiris. Two goals from Georginio Rutter, along with strikes from Jack Hinshelwood and Matt O’Riley, gave the Seagulls a comfortable 4-0 win.
 Celtic, Hearts and Palace Come Unstuck 
 There was no joy for the two Scottish Premiership sides in action last night.
 Celtic are now 33rd of 36 in the Europa League after a 4-1 hammering from Benfica. A panenka penalty from Jhon Duran got the rout underway in the fifth minute, with Vangelis Pavlidis completing the scoring late on.
 It was a better night for Hearts, but a late Nordsjaelland equaliser meant the spoils were shared in their Conference League opener.
 Finally, Crystal Palace came out on the wrong side of a topsy-turvy 3-2 defeat to Lyon in the Europa League.
 The Eagles were playing catch-up at the break, 2-0 down, before Yeremy Pino got them back into it early in the second half.
 Pavel Sulc — red-carded in Czechia's defeat to England this month — restored Lyon’s two-goal advantage in the 76th minute and held on for the win despite Daichi Kamada’s strike five minutes later.
